draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Anjuna! This village landed on the hippie trail in the late 1960s, and along with Vagator next door it's still closely tied to Goa's rave and trance culture. Its name may come from the Arabic 'Hanjuman', meaning merchant guild.
draft.hungryLine: Anjuna eats from everywhere, Goan, Israeli, Italian and French, and you can try cashew fenny, the local spirit.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Walk 8 minutes to the Sunset Viewpoint, then head up to Chapora Fort, which looks across the river to Morjim.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Try Vagator Beach just north, with black rock cliffs and three little beaches split by a headland.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Some say Anjuna's name comes from an Arabic word for 'change', because people arrived from the sea looking to change money.

legends.title: The money changers' beach
legends.body: One story says Anjuna's name comes from an Arabic word for 'change'. People used to land here from the sea looking to change money.

legends.title: Shahpoora becomes Chapora
legends.body: The fort was first called Shahpoora after Adil Shah. The Malvankars, Shivaji's naval men who stayed on in nearby villages, changed it to Shapora at the Portuguese's request.

tips.title: Hit the flea market early.
tips.body: Go early on Wednesday for bargains, rest through the hot noon hours and come back later in the day.

tips.title: Time it with a feast.
tips.body: St. Michael's Church celebrates Saint Michael on 29 September and Nossa Senhora Advogada in the second week of January.

story.title: A merchant guild's name
story.body: Historian Teresa Albuquerque traces Anjuna's name to the Arabic 'Hanjuman', meaning merchant guild. Anjuna became one of the twelve comunidades of Bardez.

story.title: A fort on the river
story.body: Adil Shah built a fort called Shahpoora high above the Chapora River. Its name later became Shapora, and today we call it Chapora Fort.

story.title: St. Michael's Church
story.body: St. Michael's Church was founded in 1595, during the long Portuguese rule. In the twentieth century the Vagator chapel became a parish church of its own, dedicated to St. Antonio.

story.title: The hippie trail
story.body: Anjuna became a stop on the hippie trail in the late 1960s. The village grew from 5,688 people in 1950 to 9,636 by 2011.

story.title: Trance and markets
story.body: Anjuna and Vagator are closely linked to rave and trance culture. The Wednesday flea market and beach shacks like Curlies keep the old spirit going.
